name: cathedral
summary: Rebuilt the east end (choir east of the transept + apse) and re-dressed both flanks in a new fix pass, parts/east-v3.mjs, run from build.mjs after towers-v2. One cross-section drives the flanks and a 5-sided apse, so chapels, piers, pinnacles and flyers run unbroken round the chevet. Apse roof: hipped half-cone in lead with polished-deepslate hips, a balustrade at its foot and a cross finial. Towers' cells (x<=22) are identical to v2; no new floating blocks; the hero, both flanks and the elevations were rendered and checked.

revisions.comment:
Owner's fix round for the Notre-Dame kit (v1 -> v2). Keep everything that works: the nave, the transepts and their rose
windows, the flying buttresses round the chevet, the lead roofs, the spire, the plot and its size, the west front's portals
and rose. Fix only the two west towers:
1. BLANK FACES. Each tower is a plain sandstone box on every face but the west: the east faces (seen from the river behind
   the cathedral, the hero view) and the north and south faces have no openings at all. Give all four faces of both towers
   the belfry stage the real towers have: two tall, narrow pointed lancet openings side by side per face in the upper third
   (dark, louvred: dark oak trapdoors or dark stained glass panes in the openings, set back one block in a deep reveal),
   with thin colonnettes (walls) between them and a pointed hood over each pair.
2. FLAT TOPS. The towers end in a flat slab. Give each top an openwork parapet (a balustrade of walls or iron bars with a
   stone rail) and a small pinnacle at each corner, and a flat lead roof set back inside it (dark).
3. FLATNESS. Break each face with horizontal string courses (a projecting stair or slab band) at the base of the belfry
   stage and under the parapet, and clasping buttresses at the corners standing proud by one block.
4. The Grand Gallery between the towers (the open colonnade at the top of the west front, linking them): if it is missing,
   add a row of slender open arches across the top of the facade between the towers, one block deep.
Keep the towers' footprint and overall height. Sandstone family as now.
revisions.summary: Both west towers fixed in a post-pass, parts/towers-v2.mjs, which build.mjs runs after the six parts. The north, east and inner faces now have a louvred belfry pair under a pointed hood, with string courses at y 69 and y 95. Free corners get clasping buttresses with spikes; the top has an openwork parapet with a slab rail, corner pinnacles and a set-back lead roof. The diff against v1 shows changes only inside the two tower boxes (x 2..23, z 6..28 and 46..68); the towers' footprint, height (y 98) and the west face are unchanged.
applied: 1 Blank faces: the north, east and inner faces of both towers (inner = the south face of the north tower, the north face of the south tower) now each have two lancets, 3 wide and y 72..88, with pointed heads of upside-down stairs. Each has an open 1-block reveal, dark oak trapdoor louvres one block back, and the dark tower interior behind them. A sandstone_wall colonnette with a cut_sandstone capital stands between the pair, and a pointed stair hood (proud 1, chiseled apex) sits over it. v1's shallow 4-wide recesses on the north and inner faces were filled in first. The west face, already louvred in v1, was left as it was.

2 Flat tops: the y 96 deck is now a deepslate_tiles lead roof with a raised deepslate_tile_slab platform set back inside it. Round its edge runs an openwork parapet: unconnected sandstone_wall balusters at y 97 under a smooth_sandstone_slab rail at y 98. Each deck corner has an end_stone pinnacle reaching y 98.

3 Flatness: projecting string courses of upside-down smooth_sandstone_stairs at y 69 (base of the belfry) and y 95 (under the parapet) on the north, east and inner faces. Clasping buttresses stand proud by 1 as an L round the NE and SE corners, and along the inner face at the SW corner; they rise to y 94 with cut_sandstone bands, and each L corner ends in an end_stone spike with a lightning_rod finial at y 98.

Checks: `mcd check` shows the same 28 floating blocks in 14 groups as v1 (the apostles and two chevet gargoyles, none in the towers). Rendered the full sheet plus two close views of the towers from NE and SE (the hero side): both towers show the belfry pairs, hoods, string courses and parapet. The south elevation shows the new belfry pair.
skipped: 4 Grande Galerie: it already exists (sandstone_wall colonnettes every 2 blocks at x 2, y 60..64, open 2 deep behind), so per the comment's 'if it is missing' nothing was added.

Clasping buttress at the outer west corners of each tower, on the north/south face: the cells at z 6 / z 68, x 2..4 fall outside the footprint mask, so no buttress was added there. The facade buttress (x 0..1) already serves that corner.
Corner pinnacles are short: the towers' height must stay at y 98, so each pinnacle rises only to y 98 (end_stone_bricks topped by an end_stone_brick_wall, or a lightning_rod on the buttress corners).

Orphans rose from 31 to 41. `check` lists only 2 orphans, both at the north transept gable (x 92..93) and present in v1, so the 10 new ones couldn't be located from its output and weren't hunted down. They are most likely the small parts added to the towers (string-course ends, lancet head stairs, rods).
The palette flags are build-wide and come from v1 (same-tone trim; dark_oak_log and moss_block outliers). Left alone because the owner asked to keep the sandstone family as it is.

revisions.comment:
Owner's fix round for the Notre-Dame kit (v2 -> v3): "this shot of the cathedral seems lacking in detail". The hero camera
looks at the EAST END and the south flank from the Seine, and from there the chevet reads as a flat, vertically striped
sandstone wall with a pale lattice on top. Read these photos first (the east end, the side the camera sees):
  /Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/mc-design-eval/benchmarks/plugin-baseline/runs/build-1/sf-landmarks/refs/paris/notre-dame/01-chevet-garden.jpg   (the chevet from Square Jean-XXIII: the hero angle)
  /Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/mc-design-eval/benchmarks/plugin-baseline/runs/build-1/sf-landmarks/refs/paris/notre-dame/02-south-seine.jpg     (the south flank from the river)
  /Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/mc-design-eval/benchmarks/plugin-baseline/runs/build-1/sf-landmarks/refs/paris/notre-dame/03-left-bank-golden.jpg
Keep the west towers and west front (v2), the spire, the transept roses, the lead roofs' colour, the plot and its size.
Rebuild the east end (the apse and the choir east of the transept) and make the south and north flanks read:
1. APSE ROOF. The apse's roof is a polygonal half-cone in dark lead, hipped round the curve from the main ridge, with a
   balustrade at its foot and a small cross or finial at the ridge's east tip.
2. CLERESTORY. Tall pointed windows (2 lancets under a round oculus, dark stained glass, deep reveals) in every bay of the
   upper apse and choir, between slender piers.
3. FLYING BUTTRESSES. Real ones: from tall outer piers capped with pinnacles (stepped, ending in a spike or a lightning
   rod), a single long sloping arch (stairs and slabs, one or two blocks thick, open underneath) spans over the aisle roof
   to the clerestory wall at each bay. Around the apse they radiate. Open air under every arch: you must see sky through
   them. No lattice grid.
4. RADIATING CHAPELS at ground level round the apse: a ring of low chapels, each with a large pointed tracery window
   (dark glass, stone mullions), a small gable over it (a steep stone triangle with a crocket edge), and a lead lean-to roof
   behind; a pierced parapet runs along their top.
5. FLANKS. Same bay rhythm along the nave and choir: aisle windows with gables, buttress piers with pinnacles, flyers.
6. RELIEF. No flat runs of more than 4 blocks on any visible face: string courses, reveals, piers proud by a block,
   dark recessed glass. Sandstone family as now (sandstone, smooth/cut/chiseled sandstone, a little end stone or birch for
   highlight), dark lead roofs.
Work on the east end and flanks only; diff should leave the towers' boxes untouched.
revisions.summary: Rebuilt the east end (choir east of the transept + apse) and re-dressed both flanks in a new fix pass, parts/east-v3.mjs, run from build.mjs after towers-v2. One cross-section drives the flanks and a 5-sided apse, so chapels, piers, pinnacles and flyers run unbroken round the chevet. Apse roof: hipped half-cone in lead with polished-deepslate hips, a balustrade at its foot and a cross finial. Towers' cells (x<=22) are identical to v2; no new floating blocks; the hero, both flanks and the elevations were rendered and checked.
applied: 1 Apse roof: 5-sided hipped half-cone continuing the main roof's pitch (ridge y 56), deepslate tiles with polished_deepslate hips, a cut_sandstone cornice and sandstone_wall balustrade at its foot (y 45-46), and a cross finial (deepslate wall + iron_bars arms + lightning rod) at the ridge's east tip.

2 Clerestory: a 2-thick wall with deep reveals (front layer left open, glass one block back). Each choir bay has twin lancets with a stone mullion under a round window (blue glass, purple heads). The apse sides are narrower and take a single lancet under a small round window. Proud pier strips mark where the flyers land.

3 Flying buttresses: tall outer piers (3 wide, set-offs at y 16/26/34) with pinnacles (3x3 cap, end-stone corner spikes, central spike, lightning-rod finial at y 48). From each pier one 1-block-thick arch: sloping stair coping on top, a curved underside of upside-down stairs, open sky under it over the aisle and tribune roofs. 4 per side on the choir, 6 per side on the nave, and 6 radiating round the apse from its corners.

4 Radiating chapels: a ring of low chapels round the apse and along the flanks, each with a pointed tracery window (5 wide where the bay allows, stone mullion, dark glass set back), a steep stone gable with stair crocket edges and an end-stone finial, a lead lean-to roof behind it, and a pierced sandstone_wall parapet between the gables.
5 Flanks: the nave and choir share the same bays - chapel window + gable, pier + pinnacle, flyer, round-headed tribune window, stepped lean-to roofs.

6 Relief: string courses every 8 blocks and cut-sandstone cornices on each band, recessed side panels on the piers, set-offs stepping the pier fronts, deep window reveals, the clerestory pier strips proud by 1, a stair cornice lip under the chapel parapet. Sandstone family + end stone accents only, dark lead roofs.

Kept as asked: west towers/front (0 changed cells at x<=22), spire, transept roses, lead roof colour, plot and size. Replaced the lights the clearing removed: floodlights at the pier feet, lanterns hung down the choir, a lantern in each chapel.
skipped: Apse windows: the 10-block apse radius leaves room for only a single 3-wide lancet under a small round window on each apse side; the twin lancets fit only in the choir bays.
Nave upper walls and roof left as they were: only the nave's side bands (chapels, aisles, piers, flyers) were rebuilt; the comment asked for the clerestory rebuild on the apse and choir.
Pier gargoyles not re-added: the clearing removed some old gargoyles that had been placed outside the plot, and the comment didn't ask for them.
The tall outer piers still read as fairly plain vertical slabs from the far hero distance; their recessed side panels only show up close.
